description: Cases separating `clear` from `reset`. Clear empties a variable for its declared type; reset puts back the value its declaration gives it. Both are answered from the declaration rather than from whatever the variable happens to hold, so a case is only useful when the declared value differs from the empty one — where the two agree, a passing case proves nothing. A `hotkey` has no empty value, so clear has no answer for one and the editor does not offer it.

cases.name: boolean
cases.reason: clear and reset agree only when the declared value is already the empty one; here they differ because the declaration says true

cases.name: color
cases.reason: a color is a JSON string, so clearing by the stored value's shape would empty it to "" instead of black

cases.name: hotkey
cases.reason: no key combination means "no key", so clear has no answer; a null clear means the operation is refused
